schemaVersion: Ehel Level 1 Intensive English Placement Exam v1.0
subject: Intensive English
title: Level 1 English Readiness Check
description: A short check of the everyday skills that help a new learner start Level 1 with confidence: reading letters and numbers, following a simple instruction, and recognising a few very common words. It does not test English grammar — that is what Level 1 itself teaches, right from the start.
attemptsAllowed: Unlimited — this exam finds your starting point; it is never a fail
feedbackMode: Immediate supportive feedback with a placement report

ready.label: Ready for Level 1
ready.message: You are ready to begin. Level 1 starts from the very beginning of English, so you do not need to know any yet — you only needed the everyday skills this check looked for.

readyWithReview.label: Ready — with a little support
readyWithReview.message: You are ready to begin Level 1. A teacher or a family member sitting with you for the first few lessons will make the start feel easier.

notReady.label: Let's start together, with support
notReady.message: Level 1 begins from zero, so there is nowhere earlier to send you — but starting alongside a teacher or a patient family member for the first unit will help far more than starting alone. Ask for that support, and begin Unit 0 whenever you are ready.

recommendation.label: Intensive English Level 1, Unit 0 with a teacher or family member

sections.title: Letters and numbers
sections.description: Recognising the letters and numbers that every Level 1 lesson uses.

sections.title: Listening and following instructions
sections.description: Following a short instruction, the way a teacher gives one in class.

sections.title: A few everyday words
sections.description: Words many people already know a little of, from travel, trade or media.

questions.question: Which one of these is a letter, not a number?
questions.explanation: B is a letter. 4, 7 and 1 are numbers. English lessons use both, so it helps to tell them apart at a glance.

questions.question: Count: 1, 2, 3, ___?
questions.explanation: After 3 comes 4. Counting in order like this comes up often in early lessons, for prices, times and ages.

questions.question: Which word is written with capital letters at the start, the way a name is written?
questions.explanation: A name starts with one capital letter, then small letters: Amina. You will write your own name this way often in Level 1.

questions.question: Which of these is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Cat, dog and bird are all words for animals. 9 is a number, so it does not belong with the others.

questions.question: Your teacher says: 'Circle the letter B.' What should you do?
questions.options: Say the letter B out loud. | Draw a ring around the letter B. | Cross out the letter B. | Write the letter B on the board.
questions.correctAnswer: Draw a ring around the letter B.
questions.explanation: To circle something means to draw a ring around it. Teachers use this word often for quick exercises.

questions.question: Your teacher says: 'Point to the door.' What should you do?
questions.options: Walk to the door and open it. | Say the word 'door' loudly. | Reach your hand towards the door. | Draw a picture of a door.
questions.correctAnswer: Reach your hand towards the door.
questions.explanation: To point means to show something with your hand or finger. It is one of the first instruction words used in class.

questions.question: A recording says: 'Listen, then repeat.' What do you do after you listen?
questions.options: Write the words down. | Say the same words again. | Wait for the next recording. | Turn the sound off.
questions.explanation: To repeat means to say it again. Listen, then repeat is exactly how Level 1's speaking practice works.

questions.question: You do not understand a question in class. What is the best thing to do?
questions.options: Say nothing and hope it passes. | Ask for it to be said again. | Answer a different question instead. | Leave the room.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask for it to be said again.
questions.explanation: Asking someone to repeat something is completely normal at the start, and Level 1 teaches you the exact words for it.

questions.question: Which word do people usually say when they meet someone?
questions.explanation: Hello is the word people say when they first meet or greet someone. Goodbye is for leaving.

questions.question: Someone asks your name. Which answer makes sense?
questions.options: My name is Amina. | It is Tuesday. | I am fine, thank you. | It costs five.
questions.explanation: A question about your name needs a name in the answer. The other answers are for different questions.

questions.question: Which word means the opposite of 'yes'?
questions.explanation: No is the opposite of yes. Okay and good are both ways of agreeing, closer in meaning to yes.

questions.question: You want something politely. Which word do you add to your request?
questions.explanation: Adding please to a request makes it polite: a glass of water, please. It is one of the very first words Level 1 teaches.
